absent: Locking rules and concurrency protection for global configuration tables and per task floating point state.
Exact numeric encodings of feature masks, leaves, register numbers and structure lengths.
Behaviour of host and guest default mask helpers and of processor capability query helpers.
Full contents and layout of register file structures beyond legacy field names used for lengths.
Details of debugging interface publication and of compaction header initialization.
Power management, signal handling and context switch paths that consume the configured sizes.
Ordering relative to jump label initialization and to later dynamic control enablement beyond the noted deferral.

findings.text: System extended processor state setup runs a single time during early boot and receives the legacy save area length for use when modern save support is unavailable, enumerates user and supervisor capabilities from the processor, builds kernel user and guest configuration records, and on success advertises compacted layout and operating system save support while on any inconsistency it falls back to legacy only operation.

Overall bring up moves from presence checks for floating point and modern save support through enumeration of user leaves and supervisor leaves, validation that core floating and vector components are present and that conflicting address extension and bound extension components are not both present, filtering by per component processor capability, gating of dynamic and supervisor sets by available instruction behaviour, derivation of default sets from host and guest masks, caching of offsets sizes and flags, computation of user kernel and guest lengths, publication of debugging interface sizes, construction of the initial state image, and a final check that the capability mask did not change before advertising operating system support, with any failure diverting to a disable path that clears capabilities and restores legacy lengths.

Public helper reports whether a requested feature set is fully contained in the kernel maximum set and optionally returns a human readable name for the most advanced requested or missing component chosen through a highest set bit search clamped to the name table length.

Public helper returns the hardware reported byte length for one extended component after emitting range warnings when the index lies before the first extended component or beyond the architectural maximum.

Public reset routine points a floating point context at its embedded default state, initializes host and guest permission records for allowed features and for kernel and user lengths, and for guest contexts selects guest defaults with architecturally reset dynamic control while for host contexts selects kernel defaults with inherited dynamic control, keeping user lengths and user feature sets identical between host and guest to preserve a common user and guest interface.
Helper locates the floating point context immediately after the task structure in memory and warns then returns a null pointer when invoked on a kernel thread.

Legacy floating point state starts at offset zero with vector state immediately after, their lengths derived from fields of the legacy register structure, and these offsets stay fixed in both standard and compacted layouts while extended components are placed later.

During cache setup each enabled extended component beyond the legacy pair records its hardware reported length and flags, components marked as supervisor keep an invalid offset marker and are excluded from the uncompacted ordering table, and the collected user components are then sorted by their uncompacted offsets so later walks tolerate hardware that reports offsets out of order.

Offset lookup returns cached values for standard layout or for legacy components, while for compacted layout it starts after the legacy area plus save header and walks enabled components in numeric order adding each length and aligning upward where flagged until reaching the target component.

Maximum capability set is reduced to an independent subset, cleared per index where the corresponding processor capability is absent with special care for index zero, stripped of dynamic user components when dynamic control is unavailable, and limited to user supported components unless supervisor save and restore behaviour is available in which case supervisor supported components are retained.

User length comes from the hardware uncompacted size query, kernel length comes from the compacted size query when compaction is enabled else equals user length, default kernel default user and guest default lengths are computed from their respective feature subsets, and length computation uses the highest enabled component with compacted offsets in compacted mode or ordered uncompacted offsets otherwise, collapsing to the base register file length when only legacy components are enabled.

Initial state construction prepares a compaction header for the default feature set, performs a boot time restore using the supervisor variant when available else the standard variant with a fault warning, assumes all extended components except legacy ones reset to zero, and captures non zero legacy initial values with a legacy save because optimized save variants skip components already in initial state.

Missing core floating vector coverage, simultaneous conflicting extension components, an initial state image larger than its static buffer, a failed length validation, or a capability mask that changed during setup each emit a diagnostic and transfer to the disable path which zeroes the feature set, clears operating system save enablement in the control register and capability flags, restores legacy lengths everywhere, clears dynamic control, and resets the current task floating point state.

Validation rejects supervisor components when supervisor save behaviour is unavailable, requires recomputed length to match hardware reported kernel length, cross checks each known component length against its matching software structure with a single warning plus leaf dump on mismatch, validates tile data per palette for title length and for product of title length with maximal tile count, and rejects unknown component numbers.

Enumeration relies on a dedicated processor identification leaf with subleaves for user size, compacted size and per component descriptors, tile topology relies on a dedicated tile leaf with subleaves per palette, supervisor enablement is manipulated through a dedicated supervisor mask register with independent bits temporarily masked during compacted size query, and layout and operating system support are advertised through processor capability flags and a control register enable bit.

Initial dynamic control mask equals the intersection of user maximum with the dynamic set, host contexts inherit that value while guest contexts start with architecturally reset dynamic control cleared, and the disable path clears dynamic control to prevent later enablement of the dynamic control branch.
Diagnostic helpers log per component offsets lengths and supported feature names during early setup without affecting functional state.
